references.text: Jesus says that his mother and his brothers are those who hear God's word and do it – a parallel statement to Luke 11:28 ([ref:Luk 8:21|Luke 8:21]).

Jesus compares the one who hears his words and acts on them with a man who builds his house on rock. To hear and keep God's word is the core of the beatitude in Luke 11:28 ([ref:Luk 6:47-49|Luke 6:47-49]).
Jesus points away from biological kinship and defines his family as those who do his heavenly Father's will – parallel to hearing and keeping God's word ([ref:Matt 12:48-50|Matthew 12:48-50]).
Jesus says: "Blessed are you if you do this" – a beatitude linked to acting in accordance with God's word, as in Luke 11:28 ([ref:Joh 13:17|John 13:17]).
James urges people to be doers of the word, not merely hearers. The one who acts on God's word is called blessed – exactly the same theme as in Luke 11:28 ([ref:Jak 1:22-25|James 1:22-25]).
A beatitude is pronounced over the one who reads, hears, and keeps the prophetic word – to hear and keep God's word, as in Luke 11:28 ([ref:Åp 1:3|Revelation 1:3]).
Blessed are those who walk according to the Lord's law and keep his testimonies – Old Testament background for the beatitude of those who hear and keep God's word ([ref:Sal 119:1-2|Psalm 119:1-2]).

Blessing is promised to those who listen to the Lord's voice and keep all his commands – a fundamental Old Testament parallel to Jesus' beatitude in Luke 11:28 ([ref:5 Mos 28:1-2|Deuteronomy 28:1-2]).

Wisdom (which points forward to Christ) says: "Blessed is the person who listens to me" – Old Testament background for the beatitude of those who hear God's word ([ref:Ordsp 8:32-34|Proverbs 8:32-34]).
"Blessed is the one who keeps the prophetic words in this book" – the final beatitude in the Bible, reflecting Luke 11:28 on keeping God's word ([ref:Åp 22:7|Revelation 22:7])
